g.text: Why no Chamfer distance is reported
A symmetric Chamfer distance between two EXACT copies of the same surface,
sampled on two independent 20,000-point direction sets, is already
1.04 % of R0 (median): this is the point-spacing floor.
The GP surfaces score 1.15–1.26 % (median by method), i.e. within about 0.2 % of
the floor, while the radial errors at identical directions are about
0.25 % (Figure H). The Chamfer metric therefore cannot discriminate the
methods at an affordable sampling density and is not used as evidence.
Normals are compared at identical directions (exact vs GP, both by the
same finite-difference rule), so they carry no point-spacing floor.
Not computed for B1/B2 (72 sparse MOOSE references, covering
radius 14.7°) or TL1 (no BO predictions exist).
Figure M (supplement). Surface-normal error of the n = 33 GP reconstructions on the analytic H1 holdout (24 Yld91 surfaces): V3 lowers the 95th-percentile normal error
(paired HL 1.48 [1.23, 1.84], 21/24); the median normal error does not differ significantly (HL 1.10 [0.92, 1.27], p = 0.26). Analytic surfaces only.
